pairs.evidence: app/features/hiring/pipeline/empty/PipelineEmptyState.tsx:92 The empty board's per-column meaning line is looked up by the stage id of the five shipped columns ("a CV lands here", "matched and scored"…), so any column a team adds or renames gets the generic 'nothing here yet', with no per-role or per-stage sentence behind it.

techniques.evidence: app/features/hiring/pipeline/empty/PipelineEmptyState.tsx:92 Meaning is keyed by the stage id and falls back to a generic line. There is no role default and no authored per-stage sentence, so custom columns get nothing.
app/features/hiring/pipeline/pipelineEventCatalog.ts:87 A board-shape move has its own event kind, separate from 'moved', with its own icon and tone (line 223).

app/features/hiring/pipeline/empty/pipelineEmptyMoves.ts:41 The inflow lane is chosen by the entry role, not by index 0 or the name 'Accepted'. Aging in pipelineRenderDiet.ts:47 also resolves through the workspace axis.

pairs.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1148 The per-job 'reached interview' rate resolves every row against the live axis only (axis = getPipelineAxis(ws).stages). Closed candidates are excluded from migration by design and keep a removed column's id, so someone interviewed and then rejected on a since-retired Interview column counts as never having advanced, even though the tombstone keeps that column's role.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1148 The gate is role-derived and inclusive (good), but a retired stage is treated as unrecognised instead of being resolved through the tombstone's role. This is the 'tombstone that resolves a label and nothing else' failure.

app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1267 Migration is one IMMEDIATE transaction with one event per candidate, refuses terminal targets before any write, and excludes all four terminal statuses. Calibration also ignores stage_migrated as evidence (line 716).
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3652 The terminal stage is reachable only with an offer_accepted outcome, resolved by role. Reject on a hired row is refused (line 3627).
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1149 Hire counts read the terminal role, not the literal 'Hired'.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1175 Occupancy is counted over the raw stage column, not joined to live stages, so off-axis occupants are counted rather than dropped.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1149 The repository layer holds no display copy.

pairs.evidence: app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:160 The screening wave, which drives irreversible auto-rejections, picks its cohort by the literal stage name 'Screened' instead of the workspace's entry/screening roles before the gate. On a board that renamed or replaced that column the wave silently acts on nobody, or on the wrong column, and nothing errors.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:160 A string comparison in a rule that drives auto-rejection. The automation-fairness backstop (line 11) also documents Python's stage == "Screened" invariant.
app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:160 Same line as above. The set where an automated screen may act should be screeningStageIds(axis) (entry/screening roles intersected with the gate), not a named column.
